study.question: Observed seed-42 full/reassigned/history-mean AUC is 0.6149816911798147/0.6147298332575719/0.6149872680212398; corresponding Logloss is 0.19656340759133067/0.196584996477262/0.19660549134391533. Whole-history reassignment loses 0.0002518579222428041 AUC versus full although it preserves row scale multisets. Whole-history averaging recovers that AUC level numerically while worsening loss. Does restricting scale allocation to the same behavior type change the reassignment penalty, and is that grouping effect different under averaging? In candidate-supplied ordered-512 diagnostics at the reassigned checkpoint, pv/cart/fav/buy event counts are 57171/1634/650/1020. Own-to-assigned scale means differ for non-pv types (cart .1848996878 to .1881117672; fav .1911590099 to .1877603233; buy .1867049336 to .1830098778). These post-training descriptive imbalances motivate a bounded grouping contrast, not a claim that cross-type movement caused the loss.
study.hypothesis: Coarse within-impression behavior-specific scale allocation may contribute to the optimization sensitivity of reassignment. Preserving each behavior group scale multiset while rotating within that group may recover some whole-history reassignment AUC loss. A behavior-group mean candidate tests preservation of between-group allocation with removal of within-group variation. The interaction between grouping and mean/reassignment discriminates a generic grouping effect from a larger grouping benefit for heterogeneous scale reassignment. This is a provisional optimization hypothesis. Neither semantic relevance nor necessity of adaptive event scales is identified.

study.proposed_difference: Two standalone modules implement action_mean_tangent (candidate.py) and action_reassigned_tangent (candidate_action_reassigned.py). For each impression p=qc*hc+qb*hb, r=sqrt(max(sum(p*p),1e-6)), u=p/r. All modes return the identical finite u. Eligible donors satisfy history_mask and sum(p*p)>=1e-6. Partition those donors by supplied history_type 1..4. The mean uses each partition mean(1/r); reassignment rotates the ordered partition by floor(n/2). All scale and coefficient derivatives are detached. For regular valid events the product-channel VJP is a_j*(g-u*(u dot g)); below the floor it remains 1000*g. Padding and unknown action codes retain the original scale; singleton partitions are unchanged. No donors cross impressions or include masked/floored events. Four group passes call the unchanged global helper; no quadratic pair matrix or new parameters. Existing history-mean and history-reassigned receipts supply the other two cells of the grouping-by-allocation 2x2, with full/fixed/DIN/raw task anchors retained. Revision of agent-r0009 prospective next action: paired seed 43/44 robustness remains consequential but is not executable through this propose interface, whose host seed is frozen at 42. Do not smuggle a seed into model configuration or train internally. This bounded two-arm discrimination replaces a redundant seed-42 replay round; no robustness conclusion follows. Append-only revision suggestion for the next authorized memory phase: record this source-verified prospective contrast alongside prior evidence, without overwriting earlier repetition plans or scientific negatives. No separate memory writer is exposed and no human-owned source is edited.
predictions: Primary descriptive mechanistic prediction: AUC(action_reassigned) - AUC(r0009-history_reassigned) > 0, with a smaller deficit to r0009-full_replay. Report exact deltas and Logloss, even if the metrics disagree; this is not a significance threshold.

Predeclared interaction D_AUC = [AUC(action_reassigned)-AUC(r0009-history_reassigned)] - [AUC(action_mean)-AUC(r0009-history_mean)] is positive if preserving behavior allocation particularly mitigates heterogeneous reassignment. Report the analogous signed D_Logloss without forcing agreement.

Action-mean may retain useful task ranking while removing within-type scale variation. Compare it against history-mean, full, fixed incumbent, DIN and aligned raw; no numerical closeness is labeled equivalence and no improvement is assumed.

Host candidate-supplied synthetic float64 VJP scaled errors should be <=1e-10 and same-state forward errors zero; sampled padding mass and empty summaries zero. Check squared-norm equality and subfloor separately. These checks do not verify all training gradients or optimizer updates.

For each impression/type, reassignment preserves scale sums and squared sums/multiset; mean preserves scale sums but changes squared sums. On float32 diagnostics expect relative conservation errors <=1e-5. Report eligible singleton/multiple events, changed fraction, within-type variance/correlation and perturbation magnitude to expose weak interventions.

Report every host run/status, capacity and measured cost; group operations may cost more. Existing 23 slices remain exploratory with sample/positive/negative counts and unsupported bins marked. Candidate-supplied first-512 diagnostics cannot establish population composition or causal mediation.
falsifiers: Nonpositive action-reassigned minus history-reassigned AUC, or an equal/larger deficit to full, weakens the proposed recovery. Nonpositive D_AUC weakens a differential grouping benefit under reassignment. Mixed directions remain unresolved; one failed implementation does not refute all grouping mechanisms.

Loss deterioration, empty/short-history or rare-type reversals contradict uniform benefit even if aggregate AUC rises. Nonpositive candidate-minus-DIN/raw contrasts weaken task utility. Do not change the frozen primary metric to select a favorable outcome.

Source/config/protocol mismatches, nonfinite output, nonzero same-state forward changes, VJP errors >1e-10 in float64 synthetic checks, donor contamination or conservation errors >1e-5 invalidate mechanistic attribution until a separately charged fix is available.

Near-zero within-type variation or a small moved fraction makes a null result weak evidence about allocation; report this rather than claiming a universal refutation. Recovery explained by singleton preservation, shorter donor distance or smaller perturbation does not establish behavior semantics.
